instruction: Select all images containing a chair.

game.semantic_variant: Select all things made for sitting on.
game.hint: Select all that apply. If you are unsure, use your best judgement.
game.explanation: Ordinary chairs count, and so do the office chair on crab legs and the armchair reading a newspaper: impossible, but still chairs. The person wearing a strapped-on chair seat and the tree stump carved into a seat are borderline cases, recorded without a verdict. The floor lamp, the chest of drawers and the clothes rail are not chairs.

correct: Correct. The Department has taken a seat to celebrate.
partial: Partially correct. Some chairs remain standing.
Partially correct. A chair has been left unattended.
incorrect: Incorrect. No policy currently exists for this kind of seating.
Incorrect. The chairs have been asked to stand down.

selection_review.reason: Nine distinct, standardised images reviewed together at tile size: two ordinary chairs (weathered wooden spindle-back chair, shallow three-quarter view; pink metal folding chair against a green wall), two impossible chairs (generated black office chair on red crab legs; generated green armchair with human arms reading a newspaper), two borderline cases (generated person on all fours wearing a chair seat and backrest; photographed tree stump carved into a high-backed seat) and three non-members (floor lamp with a pink shade, sage-green chest of drawers, free-standing clothes rail). Views, colours and settings vary within each role; generated images appear among targets and borderline cases alike, so origin does not single out the answer. The mustard armchair, the grey folding chair, the walking chair and the generated stump chair remain in the collection for later versions.
